If sentiment is positive in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment is neutral or mixed, apply a 0.2–0.5% downward adjustment for mid-horizon (8–15 days) to smooth out volatility.  
If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative streak, add a 0.5–1.0% upward bias for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum.  
If sentiment turns sharply negative after a positive streak, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias for late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, reduce forecast slope by 0.3–0.7% per day for late horizon to prevent runaway inflation.
